question: \(8^{98}\) — what is its unit digit?
explanation:
Observation
For the last digit, only the ending digit matters.

Explanation
We are doing this because the last digit repeats even when the full number becomes very large.

Replace the big base by its smaller remainder

\[
8\equiv 8\pmod{10}
\]

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 4.

\[
8\rightarrow 4\rightarrow 2\rightarrow 6
\]

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(98-1)\bmod 4+1=2
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 4.

\[
8^{98}\equiv 4\pmod{10}
\]

Answer
The 2nd term of the cycle is 4.
Therefore, the required answer is \(4\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (A).

Common Mistake
Do not use the whole base. For the last digit, only the ending digit of the base matters.

Shortcut

First make the base small, then use the power pattern.

\[
p=(98-1)\bmod 4+1=2
\]

\[
8^{98}\equiv 4\pmod{10}
\]

Fast result: \(4\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (A).

explanation.en:
Observation
For the last digit, only the ending digit matters.

We are doing this because the last digit repeats even when the full number becomes very large.

Replace the big base by its smaller remainder

\[
8\equiv 8\pmod{10}

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 4.

\[
8\rightarrow 4\rightarrow 2\rightarrow 6
\]

\[
(98-1)\bmod 4+1=2
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 4.

\[
8^{98}\equiv 4\pmod{10}

The 2nd term of the cycle is 4.
Therefore, the required answer is \(4\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (A).

Do not use the whole base. For the last digit, only the ending digit of the base matters.

\[
p=(98-1)\bmod 4+1=2
\]

\[

question: Find the smallest perfect square not less than \(400\) which leaves remainder \(9\) when divided by \(24\).
explanation:
Observation
A square is made from pairs of prime factors.

Explanation
We are doing this because every factor in a square comes in a pair.

Factorize the given number

Perfect powers are controlled by prime exponents.

\[
108=2^{2}\times 3^{3}
\]

Add only the missing prime powers

For a square, every exponent must be even.

\[
2^{2}\to 2^{2}
\]

\[
3^{3}\to 3^{4}
\]

Multiply the missing part

\[
108\times 3=324
\]

Answer
The perfect-power condition is now satisfied.
Therefore, the required answer is \(441\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (D).

Common Mistake
Do not multiply by the whole number again. For a square, add only the prime factors whose powers are unpaired.

Shortcut

Fill only the missing prime powers; do not search through squares or cubes.

\[
108\times 3=324
\]

Fast result: \(441\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (D).

stem.en: \(12^{100}\) — what is its unit digit?

explanation.en:
Observation
The clues are about digits, so place value is the main idea.

Explanation
We are doing this because digit clues become useful only after we attach them to their places.

Replace the big base by its smaller remainder

\[
12\equiv 2\pmod{10}
\]

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 4.

\[
2\rightarrow 4\rightarrow 8\rightarrow 6
\]

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(100-1)\bmod 4+1=4
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 6.

\[
12^{100}\equiv 6\pmod{10}
\]

Answer
The 4th term of the cycle is 6.
Therefore, the required answer is \(6\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (A).

Common Mistake
Do not treat every digit as having the same value. A digit in the tens place and a digit in the units place are not equal in value.

Shortcut

First make the base small, then use the power pattern.

\[
p=(100-1)\bmod 4+1=4
\]

\[
2^{100}\equiv 6\pmod{10}
\]

Fast result: \(6\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (A).

अवलोकन

व्याख्या
यह कदम इसलिए जरूरी है क्योंकि इसी से पता चलता है कि आगे कौन-सी गणना करनी है।

आधार को भाजक के अनुसार घटाएं

\[
12\equiv 2\pmod{10}
\]

शेषफल चक्र लिखें

चक्र की लंबाई = 4।

\[
2\rightarrow 4\rightarrow 8\rightarrow 6
\]

चक्र में घात की स्थिति ज्ञात करें

\[
(100-1)\bmod 4+1=4
\]

आवश्यक शेषफल पढ़ें

अतः शेषफल = 6।

\[
12^{100}\equiv 6\pmod{10}
\]

उत्तर
चक्र का 4वाँ पद 6 है।
अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प (A) है। आवश्यक मान \(6\) है।

सामान्य गलती
अक्सर गलती यह होती है कि विद्यार्थी केवल एक शर्त देखकर उत्तर चुन लेते हैं। अंतिम उत्तर को सभी शर्तों से मिलाकर जरूर देखें।

\[
p=(100-1)\bmod 4+1=4
\]

\[
2^{100}\equiv 6\pmod{10}
\]

शीघ्र परिणाम: \(6\)। अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प (A) है।

ਧਿਆਨ ਕਰੋ
ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਇਹ ਸਮਝੋ ਕਿ ਪ੍ਰਸ਼ਨ ਕਿਸ ਸੰਖਿਆ-ਨਿਯਮ ਵੱਲ ਇਸ਼ਾਰਾ ਕਰ ਰਿਹਾ ਹੈ।

ਸਮਝਾਉਣ
ਇਹ ਕਦਮ ਇਸ ਲਈ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਹੈ ਕਿਉਂਕਿ ਇਸ ਨਾਲ ਪਤਾ ਲੱਗਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਅੱਗੇ ਕਿਹੜੀ ਗਿਣਤੀ ਕਰਨੀ ਹੈ।

\[

\]

ਚੱਕਰ ਦੀ ਲੰਬਾਈ = 4।

\[
2\rightarrow 4\rightarrow 8\rightarrow 6
\]

ਚੱਕਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਘਾਤ ਦੀ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਕੱਢੋ

\[
(100-1)\bmod 4+1=4
\]

ਲੋੜੀਂਦਾ ਬਾਕੀ ਪੜ੍ਹੋ

ਇਸ ਲਈ ਬਾਕੀ = 6।

\[
12^{100}\equiv 6\pmod{10}
\]

ਉੱਤਰ
ਚੱਕਰ ਦਾ 4ਵਾਂ ਪਦ 6 ਹੈ।
ਇਸ ਲਈ ਸਹੀ ਉੱਤਰ ਵਿਕਲਪ (A) ਹੈ। ਲੋੜੀਂਦਾ ਮੁੱਲ \(6\) ਹੈ।

ਆਧਾਰ ਇੱਕ ਵਾਰ ਘਟਾ ਕੇ ਚੱਕਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਘਾਤ ਦੀ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਤੇ ਜਾਓ।

\[
p=(100-1)\bmod 4+1=4
\]

\[
2^{100}\equiv 6\pmod{10}
\]

ਛੇਤੀ ਨਤੀਜਾ: \(6\)। ਇਸ ਲਈ ਸਹੀ ਉੱਤਰ ਵਿਕਲਪ (A) ਹੈ।

question: Find the smallest integer above \(117\) which is a common multiple of \(12\) and \(6\).
explanation:
Observation
The question asks for the best number that still follows the given rule.

Explanation
We are doing this because testing numbers one by one is slow; the pattern tells us where to look.

Put the given conditions together first

First combine the divisibility facts. A number divisible by each given divisor must be a multiple of their LCM.

\[
m=12
\]

Now choose the number that stays within the given limit

Now use the nearby multiples and choose the first or last one according to the question.

\[
q=\left\lceil\frac{118}{12}\right\rceil
\]

\[
12\times q=120
\]

Answer
The selected number is 120, and it satisfies the required divisibility condition.
Therefore, the required answer is \(120\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (A).

Common Mistake
Do not start testing random numbers. First find the repeating number pattern, then move to the nearest allowed value.

Shortcut

Take the LCM once, then jump directly to the nearest multiple asked in the question.

\[
12\times q=120
\]

Fast result: \(120\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (A).

question: What is the smallest number that is divisible by both \(60\) and \(195\)?
explanation:
Observation
HCF means the greatest part common to all numbers.

Explanation
We are doing this because only the part common to all numbers can remain in the HCF.

Write prime factorizations

\[
60=2^{2}\times 3\times 5
\]

\[
195=3\times 5\times 13
\]

Take highest powers for LCM

\[
\operatorname{LCM}(60,195)=780
\]

Answer
The LCM is 780.
Therefore, the required answer is \(780\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (A).

Common Mistake
Do not take the highest powers for HCF. HCF takes only the common primes with the smaller powers.

Shortcut

Use the product identity with the HCF.

\[
\operatorname{LCM}(60,195)=\frac{60\times 195}{\operatorname{HCF}(60,195)}=780
\]

Fast result: \(780\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (A).

Observation
HCF means the greatest part common to all numbers.

Explanation
We are doing this because only the part common to all numbers can remain in the HCF.

Write prime factorizations

\[
60=2^{2}\times 3\times 5
\]

\[
195=3\times 5\times 13
\]

Take highest powers for LCM

\[
\operatorname{LCM}(60,195)=780
\]

Answer
The LCM is 780.
Therefore, the required answer is \(780\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (A).

Common Mistake
Do not take the highest powers for HCF. HCF takes only the common primes with the smaller powers.

Shortcut

Use the product identity with the HCF.

\[
\operatorname{LCM}(60,195)=\frac{60\times 195}{\operatorname{HCF}(60,195)}=780
\]

Fast result: \(780\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (A).

question: By what least number should \(108\) be multiplied to make it a perfect square?
explanation:
Observation
A square is made from pairs of prime factors.

Explanation
We are doing this because every factor in a square comes in a pair.

Factorize the given number

Perfect powers are controlled by prime exponents.

\[
108=2^{2}\times 3^{3}
\]

Add only the missing prime powers

For a square, every exponent must be even.

\[
2^{2}\to 2^{2}
\]

\[
3^{3}\to 3^{4}
\]

Multiply the missing part

\[
108\times 3=324
\]

Answer
The perfect-power condition is now satisfied.
Therefore, the required answer is \(3\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (A).

Common Mistake
Do not multiply by the whole number again. For a square, add only the prime factors whose powers are unpaired.

Shortcut

Fill only the missing prime powers; do not search through squares or cubes.

\[
108\times 3=324
\]

Fast result: \(3\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (A).

en.question: By what least number should \(108\) be multiplied to make it a perfect square?
en.explanation:
Observation
A square is made from pairs of prime factors.

Explanation
We are doing this because every factor in a square comes in a pair.

Factorize the given number

Perfect powers are controlled by prime exponents.

\[
108=2^{2}\times 3^{3}
\]

Add only the missing prime powers

For a square, every exponent must be even.

\[
2^{2}\to 2^{2}
\]

\[
3^{3}\to 3^{4}
\]

Multiply the missing part

\[
108\times 3=324
\]

Answer
The perfect-power condition is now satisfied.
Therefore, the required answer is \(3\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (A).

Common Mistake
Do not multiply by the whole number again. For a square, add only the prime factors whose powers are unpaired.

Shortcut

Fill only the missing prime powers; do not search through squares or cubes.

\[
108\times 3=324
\]

Fast result: \(3\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (A).

question: Find the last digit of \(17^{70}\).
explanation:
Observation
For the last digit, only the ending digit matters.

Explanation
We are doing this because the last digit repeats even when the full number becomes very large.

Replace the big base by its smaller remainder

\[
17\equiv 7\pmod{10}
\]

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 4.

\[
7\rightarrow 9\rightarrow 3\rightarrow 1
\]

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(70-1)\bmod 4+1=2
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 9.

\[
17^{70}\equiv 9\pmod{10}
\]

Answer
The 2nd term of the cycle is 9.
Therefore, the required answer is \(9\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (C).

Common Mistake
Do not use the whole base. For the last digit, only the ending digit of the base matters.

Shortcut

First make the base small, then use the power pattern.

\[
p=(70-1)\bmod 4+1=2
\]

\[
7^{70}\equiv 9\pmod{10}
\]

Fast result: \(9\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (C).

stem.en: Find the last digit of \(17^{70}\).

explanation.en:
Observation
For the last digit, only the ending digit matters.

Explanation
We are doing this because the last digit repeats even when the full number becomes very large.

Replace the big base by its smaller remainder

\[
17\equiv 7\pmod{10}
\]

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 4.

\[
7\rightarrow 9\rightarrow 3\rightarrow 1
\]

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(70-1)\bmod 4+1=2
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 9.

\[
17^{70}\equiv 9\pmod{10}
\]

Answer
The 2nd term of the cycle is 9.
Therefore, the required answer is \(9\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (C).

Common Mistake
Do not use the whole base. For the last digit, only the ending digit of the base matters.

Shortcut

First make the base small, then use the power pattern.

\[
p=(70-1)\bmod 4+1=2
\]

\[
7^{70}\equiv 9\pmod{10}
\]

Fast result: \(9\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (C).

question: By what least number should \(180\) be multiplied to make it a perfect square?
explanation:
Observation
A square is made from pairs of prime factors.

Explanation
We are doing this because every factor in a square comes in a pair.

Factorize the given number

Perfect powers are controlled by prime exponents.

\[
180=2^{2}\times 3^{2}\times 5
\]

Add only the missing prime powers

For a square, every exponent must be even.

\[
2^{2}\to 2^{2}
\]

\[
3^{2}\to 3^{2}
\]

\[
5^{1}\to 5^{2}
\]

Multiply the missing part

\[
180\times 5=900
\]

Answer
The perfect-power condition is now satisfied.
Therefore, the required answer is \(5\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (C).

Common Mistake
Do not multiply by the whole number again. For a square, add only the prime factors whose powers are unpaired.

Shortcut

Fill only the missing prime powers; do not search through squares or cubes.

\[
180\times 5=900
\]

Fast result: \(5\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (C).

A square is made from pairs of prime factors.

We are doing this because every factor in a square comes in a pair.

Factorize the given number

Perfect powers are controlled by prime exponents.

Add only the missing prime powers

\[

\]

The perfect-power condition is now satisfied.

Do not multiply by the whole number again. For a square, add only the prime factors whose powers are unpaired.

\[
180\times 5=900
\]

question: Find the remainder: \(3^{61} \div 9\).
explanation:
Observation
The question is about what is left after division.

Explanation
We are doing this because numbers with the same remainder move in equal jumps.

Replace the big base by its smaller remainder

\[
3\equiv 3\pmod{9}
\]

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 2.

\[
3\rightarrow 0
\]

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(61-1)\bmod 2+1=1
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 3.

\[
3^{61}\equiv 3\pmod{9}
\]

Answer
The 1st term of the cycle is 3.
Therefore, the required answer is \(0\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (C).

Common Mistake
Do not count from zero blindly. Check whether the lower and upper limits are included in the given range.

Shortcut

First make the base small, then use the power pattern.

\[
p=(61-1)\bmod 2+1=1
\]

\[
3^{61}\equiv 3\pmod{9}
\]

Fast result: \(0\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (C).

en.question: Find the remainder: \(3^{61} \div 9\).
en.explanation:
Observation
The question is about what is left after division.

Explanation
We are doing this because numbers with the same remainder move in equal jumps.

Replace the big base by its smaller remainder

\[
3\equiv 3\pmod{9}
\]

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 2.

\[
3\rightarrow 0
\]

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(61-1)\bmod 2+1=1
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 3.

\[
3^{61}\equiv 3\pmod{9}
\]

Answer
The 1st term of the cycle is 3.
Therefore, the required answer is \(0\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (C).

Common Mistake
Do not count from zero blindly. Check whether the lower and upper limits are included in the given range.

Shortcut

First make the base small, then use the power pattern.

\[
p=(61-1)\bmod 2+1=1
\]

\[
3^{61}\equiv 3\pmod{9}
\]

Fast result: \(0\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (C).

hi.explanation:
अवलोकन
पहले यह समझें कि प्रश्न किस संख्या-नियम की तरफ इशारा कर रहा है।

व्याख्या
यह कदम इसलिए जरूरी है क्योंकि इसी से पता चलता है कि आगे कौन-सी गणना करनी है।

आधार को भाजक के अनुसार घटाएं

\[

\]

शेषफल चक्र लिखें

चक्र की लंबाई = 2।

\[
3\rightarrow 0
\]

चक्र में घात की स्थिति ज्ञात करें

\[
(61-1)\bmod 2+1=1
\]

आवश्यक शेषफल पढ़ें

अतः शेषफल = 3।

\[
3^{61}\equiv 3\pmod{9}
\]

उत्तर
चक्र का 1वाँ पद 3 है।
अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प (C) है। आवश्यक मान \(0\) है।

सामान्य गलती
अक्सर गलती यह होती है कि विद्यार्थी केवल एक शर्त देखकर उत्तर चुन लेते हैं। अंतिम उत्तर को सभी शर्तों से मिलाकर जरूर देखें।

शॉर्टकट

आधार एक बार घटाकर चक्र में घात की स्थिति पर जाएं।

\[
p=(61-1)\bmod 2+1=1
\]

\[
3^{61}\equiv 3\pmod{9}
\]

शीघ्र परिणाम: \(0\)। अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प (C) है।

question: What is the least perfect cube that is divisible by \(135\)?
explanation:
Observation
A cube is made from groups of three equal prime factors.

Explanation
We are doing this because every factor in a cube comes in a group of three.

Factorize the given number

Perfect powers are controlled by prime exponents.

\[
135=3^{3}\times 5
\]

Add only the missing prime powers

For a cube, every exponent must be a multiple of 3.

\[
3^{3}\to 3^{3}
\]

\[
5^{1}\to 5^{3}
\]

Multiply the missing part

\[
135\times 25=3375
\]

Answer
The perfect-power condition is now satisfied.
Therefore, the required answer is \(3375\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (C).

Common Mistake
Do not stop after making exponents even. For a cube, every prime power must be grouped in threes.

Shortcut

Fill only the missing prime powers; do not search through squares or cubes.

\[
135\times 25=3375
\]

Fast result: \(3375\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (C).

explanation.en:
Observation
A cube is made from groups of three equal prime factors.

Explanation
We are doing this because every factor in a cube comes in a group of three.

Factorize the given number

Perfect powers are controlled by prime exponents.

\[
135=3^{3}\times 5
\]

Add only the missing prime powers

For a cube, every exponent must be a multiple of 3.

\[
3^{3}\to 3^{3}
\]

\[
5^{1}\to 5^{3}
\]

Multiply the missing part

\[
135\times 25=3375
\]

Answer
The perfect-power condition is now satisfied.
Therefore, the required answer is \(3375\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (C).

Common Mistake
Do not stop after making exponents even. For a cube, every prime power must be grouped in threes.

Shortcut

Fill only the missing prime powers; do not search through squares or cubes.

\[
135\times 25=3375
\]

Fast result: \(3375\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (C).

question: Bells ring at intervals of \(36\) and \(153\) minutes. After how many minutes will both ring together again?
explanation:
Observation
LCM must be a multiple of every given number.

Explanation
We are doing this because the LCM must have enough factors to cover every given number.

Write prime factorizations

\[
36=2^{2}\times 3^{2}
\]

\[
153=3^{2}\times 17
\]

Take highest powers for LCM

\[
\operatorname{LCM}(36,153)=612
\]

Answer
The LCM is 612.
Therefore, the required answer is \(612\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (C).

Common Mistake
Do not take only common primes for LCM. LCM must include every prime needed by any of the numbers.

Shortcut

Use the product identity with the HCF.

\[
\operatorname{LCM}(36,153)=\frac{36\times 153}{\operatorname{HCF}(36,153)}=612
\]

Fast result: \(612\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (C).

stepwiseExplanation.en:
Observation
LCM must be a multiple of every given number.

Explanation
We are doing this because the LCM must have enough factors to cover every given number.

Write prime factorizations

\[
36=2^{2}\times 3^{2}
\]

\[
153=3^{2}\times 17
\]

Take highest powers for LCM

\[
\operatorname{LCM}(36,153)=612
\]

Answer
The LCM is 612.
Therefore, the required answer is \(612\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (C).

Common Mistake
Do not take only common primes for LCM. LCM must include every prime needed by any of the numbers.

Shortcut

Use the product identity with the HCF.

\[
\operatorname{LCM}(36,153)=\frac{36\times 153}{\operatorname{HCF}(36,153)}=612
\]

Fast result: \(612\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (C).

अवलोकन

\[

\[

\[

\]

अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प (C) है। आवश्यक मान \(612\) है।

सामान्य गलती
अक्सर गलती यह होती है कि विद्यार्थी केवल एक शर्त देखकर उत्तर चुन लेते हैं। अंतिम उत्तर को सभी शर्तों से मिलाकर जरूर देखें।

HCF के साथ गुणन पहचान लगाएं।

\[

question: What is the remainder when \(7^{77}\) is divided by \(19\)?
explanation:
Observation
This question mixes more than one number-system idea.

Explanation
We are doing this because each clue reduces the choices for the next clue.

Replace the big base by its smaller remainder

\[
7\equiv 7\pmod{19}
\]

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 3.

\[
7\rightarrow 11\rightarrow 1
\]

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(77-1)\bmod 3+1=2
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 11.

\[
7^{77}\equiv 11\pmod{19}
\]

Answer
The 2nd term of the cycle is 11.
Therefore, the required answer is \(11\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (D).

Common Mistake
Do not solve only the first clue. The final answer must satisfy every condition in the question.

Shortcut

First make the base small, then use the power pattern.

\[
p=(77-1)\bmod 3+1=2
\]

\[
7^{77}\equiv 11\pmod{19}
\]

Fast result: \(11\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (D).

pa.question: \(7^{77}\) ਨੂੰ \(19\) ਨਾਲ ਭਾਗ ਦੇਣ ਤੇ ਬਾਕੀ ਕੀ ਹੈ?
pa.explanation:
ਧਿਆਨ ਕਰੋ
ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਇਹ ਸਮਝੋ ਕਿ ਪ੍ਰਸ਼ਨ ਕਿਸ ਸੰਖਿਆ-ਨਿਯਮ ਵੱਲ ਇਸ਼ਾਰਾ ਕਰ ਰਿਹਾ ਹੈ।

ਆਧਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਭਾਜਕ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਘਟਾਓ

\[
7\equiv 7\pmod{19}
\]

ਬਾਕੀ ਚੱਕਰ ਲਿਖੋ

ਚੱਕਰ ਦੀ ਲੰਬਾਈ = 3।

\[
7\rightarrow 11\rightarrow 1
\]

ਚੱਕਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਘਾਤ ਦੀ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਕੱਢੋ

\[
(77-1)\bmod 3+1=2
\]

ਲੋੜੀਂਦਾ ਬਾਕੀ ਪੜ੍ਹੋ

ਇਸ ਲਈ ਬਾਕੀ = 11।

\[
7^{77}\equiv 11\pmod{19}
\]

ਉੱਤਰ
ਚੱਕਰ ਦਾ 2ਵਾਂ ਪਦ 11 ਹੈ।
ਇਸ ਲਈ ਸਹੀ ਉੱਤਰ ਵਿਕਲਪ (D) ਹੈ। ਲੋੜੀਂਦਾ ਮੁੱਲ \(11\) ਹੈ।

ਆਮ ਗਲਤੀ
ਅਕਸਰ ਗਲਤੀ ਇਹ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਵਿਦਿਆਰਥੀ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਇੱਕ ਸ਼ਰਤ ਦੇਖ ਕੇ ਉੱਤਰ ਚੁਣ ਲੈਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਅੰਤਿਮ ਉੱਤਰ ਨੂੰ ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਸ਼ਰਤਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਜ਼ਰੂਰ ਮਿਲਾਓ।

ਛੋਟਾ ਤਰੀਕਾ

ਆਧਾਰ ਇੱਕ ਵਾਰ ਘਟਾ ਕੇ ਚੱਕਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਘਾਤ ਦੀ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਤੇ ਜਾਓ।

\[
p=(77-1)\bmod 3+1=2
\]

\[
7^{77}\equiv 11\pmod{19}
\]

ਛੇਤੀ ਨਤੀਜਾ: \(11\)। ਇਸ ਲਈ ਸਹੀ ਉੱਤਰ ਵਿਕਲਪ (D) ਹੈ।

question: How many factors does \(36\) have?
explanation:
Observation
The question is about what is left after division.

Explanation
We are doing this because numbers with the same remainder move in equal jumps.

Write prime factorization

\[
36=2^{2}\times 3^{2}
\]

For each prime power, count all choices from zero up to that exponent

Each exponent contributes one more choice than its value.

\[
d(36)=(2+1)\times (2+1)=9
\]

Answer
The number of positive divisors is 9.
Therefore, the required answer is \(9\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (D).

Common Mistake
Do not count from zero blindly. Check whether the lower and upper limits are included in the given range.

Shortcut

Multiply (exponent + 1) across all prime powers.

\[
(2+1)\times (2+1)
\]

Fast result: \(9\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (D).

ਇਹ ਕਦਮ ਇਸ ਲਈ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਹੈ ਕਿਉਂਕਿ ਇਸ ਨਾਲ ਪਤਾ ਲੱਗਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਅੱਗੇ ਕਿਹੜੀ ਗਿਣਤੀ ਕਰਨੀ ਹੈ।

ਅਭਾਜ ਗੁਣਨਖੰਡ ਲਿਖੋ

\[
36=2^{2}\times 3^{2}
\]

ਘਾਤਾਂ ਤੇ (+1) ਨਿਯਮ ਲਗਾਓ

ਹਰ ਘਾਤ ਆਪਣੇ ਮੁੱਲ ਤੋਂ ਇੱਕ ਵੱਧ ਵਿਕਲਪ ਦਿੰਦੀ ਹੈ।

\[
d(36)=(2+1)\times (2+1)=9
\]

ਉੱਤਰ
ਧਨਾਤਮਕ ਭਾਜਕਾਂ ਦੀ ਗਿਣਤੀ 9 ਹੈ।
ਇਸ ਲਈ ਸਹੀ ਉੱਤਰ ਵਿਕਲਪ (D) ਹੈ। ਲੋੜੀਂਦਾ ਮੁੱਲ \(9\) ਹੈ।

ਆਮ ਗਲਤੀ
ਅਕਸਰ ਗਲਤੀ ਇਹ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਵਿਦਿਆਰਥੀ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਇੱਕ ਸ਼ਰਤ ਦੇਖ ਕੇ ਉੱਤਰ ਚੁਣ ਲੈਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਅੰਤਿਮ ਉੱਤਰ ਨੂੰ ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਸ਼ਰਤਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਜ਼ਰੂਰ ਮਿਲਾਓ।

ਛੋਟਾ ਤਰੀਕਾ

ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਅਭਾਜ ਘਾਤਾਂ ਤੇ (ਘਾਤ + 1) ਦਾ ਗੁਣਨ ਕਰੋ।

\[
(2+1)\times (2+1)
\]

ਛੇਤੀ ਨਤੀਜਾ: \(9\)। ਇਸ ਲਈ ਸਹੀ ਉੱਤਰ ਵਿਕਲਪ (D) ਹੈ।

en.question: How many factors does \(36\) have?
en.explanation:
Observation
The question is about what is left after division.

Explanation
We are doing this because numbers with the same remainder move in equal jumps.

Write prime factorization

\[
36=2^{2}\times 3^{2}
\]

For each prime power, count all choices from zero up to that exponent

Each exponent contributes one more choice than its value.

\[
d(36)=(2+1)\times (2+1)=9
\]

Answer
The number of positive divisors is 9.
Therefore, the required answer is \(9\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (D).

Common Mistake
Do not count from zero blindly. Check whether the lower and upper limits are included in the given range.

Shortcut

Multiply (exponent + 1) across all prime powers.

\[
(2+1)\times (2+1)
\]

Fast result: \(9\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (D).

hi.question: \(36\) के कुल कितने भाजक हैं?
hi.explanation:
अवलोकन
पहले यह समझें कि प्रश्न किस संख्या-नियम की तरफ इशारा कर रहा है।

व्याख्या
यह कदम इसलिए जरूरी है क्योंकि इसी से पता चलता है कि आगे कौन-सी गणना करनी है।

अभाज्य गुणनखंड लिखें

\[
36=2^{2}\times 3^{2}
\]

घातों पर (+1) नियम लगाएं

प्रत्येक घात अपने मान से एक अधिक विकल्प देती है।

\[
d(36)=(2+1)\times (2+1)=9
\]

उत्तर
धनात्मक भाजकों की संख्या 9 है।
अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प (D) है। आवश्यक मान \(9\) है।

सामान्य गलती
अक्सर गलती यह होती है कि विद्यार्थी केवल एक शर्त देखकर उत्तर चुन लेते हैं। अंतिम उत्तर को सभी शर्तों से मिलाकर जरूर देखें।

शॉर्टकट

सभी अभाज्य घातों पर (घात + 1) का गुणन करें।

\[
(2+1)\times (2+1)
\]

शीघ्र परिणाम: \(9\)। अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प (D) है।

\[

question: What is the least perfect square that is divisible by \(200\)?
explanation:
Observation
A square is made from pairs of prime factors.

Explanation
We are doing this because every factor in a square comes in a pair.

Factorize the given number

Perfect powers are controlled by prime exponents.

\[
200=2^{3}\times 5^{2}
\]

Add only the missing prime powers

For a square, every exponent must be even.

\[
2^{3}\to 2^{4}
\]

\[
5^{2}\to 5^{2}
\]

Multiply the missing part

\[
200\times 2=400
\]

Answer
The perfect-power condition is now satisfied.
Therefore, the required answer is \(400\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (D).

Common Mistake
Do not multiply by the whole number again. For a square, add only the prime factors whose powers are unpaired.

Shortcut

Fill only the missing prime powers; do not search through squares or cubes.

\[
200\times 2=400
\]

Fast result: \(400\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (D).

question: \(2^{95}\) — what are its last three digits?
explanation:
Observation
The clues are about digits, so place value is the main idea.

Explanation
We are doing this because digit clues become useful only after we attach them to their places.

Replace the big base by its smaller remainder

\[
2\equiv 2\pmod{1000}
\]

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 24.

\[
2\rightarrow 4\rightarrow 8\rightarrow 16\rightarrow 32\rightarrow 64\rightarrow 128\rightarrow 256\rightarrow 512\rightarrow 24\rightarrow 48\rightarrow 96\rightarrow 192\rightarrow 384\rightarrow 768\rightarrow 536\rightarrow 72\rightarrow 144\rightarrow 288\rightarrow 576\rightarrow 152\rightarrow 304\rightarrow 608\rightarrow 216
\]

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(95-1)\bmod 24+1=23
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 608.

\[
2^{95}\equiv 608\pmod{1000}
\]

Answer
The 23th term of the cycle is 608.
Therefore, the required answer is \(168\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (A).

Common Mistake
Do not treat every digit as having the same value. A digit in the tens place and a digit in the units place are not equal in value.

Shortcut

First make the base small, then use the power pattern.

\[
p=(95-1)\bmod 24+1=23
\]

\[
2^{95}\equiv 608\pmod{1000}
\]

Fast result: \(168\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (A).

ਇਹ ਕਦਮ ਇਸ ਲਈ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਹੈ ਕਿਉਂਕਿ ਇਸ ਨਾਲ ਪਤਾ ਲੱਗਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਅੱਗੇ ਕਿਹੜੀ ਗਿਣਤੀ ਕਰਨੀ ਹੈ।

ਆਧਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਭਾਜਕ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਘਟਾਓ

\[
2\equiv 2\pmod{1000}
\]

ਬਾਕੀ ਚੱਕਰ ਲਿਖੋ

ਚੱਕਰ ਦੀ ਲੰਬਾਈ = 24।

\[
2\rightarrow 4\rightarrow 8\rightarrow 16\rightarrow 32\rightarrow 64\rightarrow 128\rightarrow 256\rightarrow 512\rightarrow 24\rightarrow 48\rightarrow 96\rightarrow 192\rightarrow 384\rightarrow 768\rightarrow 536\rightarrow 72\rightarrow 144\rightarrow 288\rightarrow 576\rightarrow 152\rightarrow 304\rightarrow 608\rightarrow 216
\]

ਚੱਕਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਘਾਤ ਦੀ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਕੱਢੋ

\[
(95-1)\bmod 24+1=23
\]

ਲੋੜੀਂਦਾ ਬਾਕੀ ਪੜ੍ਹੋ

ਇਸ ਲਈ ਬਾਕੀ = 608।

\[
2^{95}\equiv 608\pmod{1000}
\]

ਉੱਤਰ
ਚੱਕਰ ਦਾ 23ਵਾਂ ਪਦ 608 ਹੈ।
ਇਸ ਲਈ ਸਹੀ ਉੱਤਰ ਵਿਕਲਪ (A) ਹੈ। ਲੋੜੀਂਦਾ ਮੁੱਲ \(168\) ਹੈ।

ਆਮ ਗਲਤੀ
ਅਕਸਰ ਗਲਤੀ ਇਹ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਵਿਦਿਆਰਥੀ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਇੱਕ ਸ਼ਰਤ ਦੇਖ ਕੇ ਉੱਤਰ ਚੁਣ ਲੈਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਅੰਤਿਮ ਉੱਤਰ ਨੂੰ ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਸ਼ਰਤਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਜ਼ਰੂਰ ਮਿਲਾਓ।

ਛੋਟਾ ਤਰੀਕਾ

ਆਧਾਰ ਇੱਕ ਵਾਰ ਘਟਾ ਕੇ ਚੱਕਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਘਾਤ ਦੀ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਤੇ ਜਾਓ।

\[
p=(95-1)\bmod 24+1=23
\]

\[
2^{95}\equiv 608\pmod{1000}
\]

ਛੇਤੀ ਨਤੀਜਾ: \(168\)। ਇਸ ਲਈ ਸਹੀ ਉੱਤਰ ਵਿਕਲਪ (A) ਹੈ।

stepwiseExplanation.en:
Observation
The clues are about digits, so place value is the main idea.

Explanation
We are doing this because digit clues become useful only after we attach them to their places.

Replace the big base by its smaller remainder

\[
2\equiv 2\pmod{1000}
\]

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 24.

\[
2\rightarrow 4\rightarrow 8\rightarrow 16\rightarrow 32\rightarrow 64\rightarrow 128\rightarrow 256\rightarrow 512\rightarrow 24\rightarrow 48\rightarrow 96\rightarrow 192\rightarrow 384\rightarrow 768\rightarrow 536\rightarrow 72\rightarrow 144\rightarrow 288\rightarrow 576\rightarrow 152\rightarrow 304\rightarrow 608\rightarrow 216
\]

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(95-1)\bmod 24+1=23
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 608.

\[
2^{95}\equiv 608\pmod{1000}
\]

Answer
The 23th term of the cycle is 608.
Therefore, the required answer is \(168\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (A).

Common Mistake
Do not treat every digit as having the same value. A digit in the tens place and a digit in the units place are not equal in value.

Shortcut

First make the base small, then use the power pattern.

\[
p=(95-1)\bmod 24+1=23
\]

\[
2^{95}\equiv 608\pmod{1000}
\]

Fast result: \(168\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (A).

अवलोकन
पहले यह समझें कि प्रश्न किस संख्या-नियम की तरफ इशारा कर रहा है।

व्याख्या
यह कदम इसलिए जरूरी है क्योंकि इसी से पता चलता है कि आगे कौन-सी गणना करनी है।

आधार को भाजक के अनुसार घटाएं

\[
2\equiv 2\pmod{1000}
\]

शेषफल चक्र लिखें

चक्र की लंबाई = 24।

\[
2\rightarrow 4\rightarrow 8\rightarrow 16\rightarrow 32\rightarrow 64\rightarrow 128\rightarrow 256\rightarrow 512\rightarrow 24\rightarrow 48\rightarrow 96\rightarrow 192\rightarrow 384\rightarrow 768\rightarrow 536\rightarrow 72\rightarrow 144\rightarrow 288\rightarrow 576\rightarrow 152\rightarrow 304\rightarrow 608\rightarrow 216
\]

चक्र में घात की स्थिति ज्ञात करें

\[
(95-1)\bmod 24+1=23
\]

आवश्यक शेषफल पढ़ें

अतः शेषफल = 608।

\[
2^{95}\equiv 608\pmod{1000}
\]

उत्तर
चक्र का 23वाँ पद 608 है।
अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प (A) है। आवश्यक मान \(168\) है।

सामान्य गलती
अक्सर गलती यह होती है कि विद्यार्थी केवल एक शर्त देखकर उत्तर चुन लेते हैं। अंतिम उत्तर को सभी शर्तों से मिलाकर जरूर देखें।

शॉर्टकट

आधार एक बार घटाकर चक्र में घात की स्थिति पर जाएं।

\[
p=(95-1)\bmod 24+1=23
\]

\[
2^{95}\equiv 608\pmod{1000}
\]

शीघ्र परिणाम: \(168\)। अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प (A) है।

question: Find the remainder: \(11^{72} \div 11\).
explanation:
Observation
The question is about what is left after division.

Explanation
We are doing this because numbers with the same remainder move in equal jumps.

Replace the big base by its smaller remainder

\[
11\equiv 0\pmod{11}
\]

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 1.

\[
0
\]

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(72-1)\bmod 1+1=1
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 0.

\[
11^{72}\equiv 0\pmod{11}
\]

Answer
The 1st term of the cycle is 0.
Therefore, the required answer is \(0\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (C).

Common Mistake
Do not count from zero blindly. Check whether the lower and upper limits are included in the given range.

Shortcut

First make the base small, then use the power pattern.

\[
p=(72-1)\bmod 1+1=1
\]

\[
0^{72}\equiv 0\pmod{11}
\]

Fast result: \(0\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (C).

question: \(2^{44}\) is divided by \(11\). What is the remainder?
explanation:
Observation
The question is about what is left after division.

Explanation
We are doing this because numbers with the same remainder move in equal jumps.

Replace the big base by its smaller remainder

\[
2\equiv 2\pmod{11}
\]

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 10.

\[
2\rightarrow 4\rightarrow 8\rightarrow 5\rightarrow 10\rightarrow 9\rightarrow 7\rightarrow 3\rightarrow 6\rightarrow 1
\]

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(44-1)\bmod 10+1=4
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 5.

\[
2^{44}\equiv 5\pmod{11}
\]

Answer
The 4th term of the cycle is 5.
Therefore, the required answer is \(5\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (A).

Common Mistake
Do not count from zero blindly. Check whether the lower and upper limits are included in the given range.

Shortcut

First make the base small, then use the power pattern.

\[
p=(44-1)\bmod 10+1=4
\]

\[
2^{44}\equiv 5\pmod{11}
\]

Fast result: \(5\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (A).

stem.en: \(2^{44}\) is divided by \(11\). What is the remainder?

explanation.en:
Observation
The question is about what is left after division.

Explanation
We are doing this because numbers with the same remainder move in equal jumps.

Replace the big base by its smaller remainder

\[
2\equiv 2\pmod{11}
\]

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 10.

\[
2\rightarrow 4\rightarrow 8\rightarrow 5\rightarrow 10\rightarrow 9\rightarrow 7\rightarrow 3\rightarrow 6\rightarrow 1
\]

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(44-1)\bmod 10+1=4
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 5.

\[
2^{44}\equiv 5\pmod{11}
\]

Answer
The 4th term of the cycle is 5.
Therefore, the required answer is \(5\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (A).

Common Mistake
Do not count from zero blindly. Check whether the lower and upper limits are included in the given range.

First make the base small, then use the power pattern.

\[
p=(44-1)\bmod 10+1=4
\]

\[

\]

question: Count the numbers between \(123\) and \(280\) that are exactly divisible by \(6\).
explanation:
Observation
A missing digit is decided by the number rule given in the question.

Explanation
We are doing this because the right digit must make the whole number satisfy the given rule.

Find the first valid multiple

Therefore, the first multiple of 6 greater than 123 is 126.

\[
6\times 21=126
\]

Find the last valid multiple

Therefore, 276 is the greatest multiple of 6 not exceeding 280.

\[
280=6\times 46+4
\]

\[
280-4=276
\]

Count the valid multiples

The multiples form an arithmetic progression with common difference 6.

\[
\frac{276-126}{6}+1=25+1=26
\]

Answer
The total number of multiples is 26.
Hence, there are 26 multiples of 6 in the given range.
Therefore, the required answer is \(26\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (C).

Common Mistake
Many students stop as soon as they find a digit. Always put the digit back into the whole number and check the rule again.

Shortcut

Count multiples using quotient floors on the range limits.

\[
\left\lfloor\frac{280}{6}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\frac{122}{6}\right\rfloor
\]

\[
46-20=26
\]

Fast result: \(26\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (C).

question: The number \(292x6\) is divisible by \(12\). What is the value of \(x\)?
explanation:
Observation
This question mixes more than one number-system idea.

Explanation
We are doing this because each clue reduces the choices for the next clue.

Split the rule for 12

A number divisible by 12 must be divisible by both 3 and 4.

\[
N\equiv 0\pmod{3}
\]

\[
N\equiv 0\pmod{4}
\]

Use the digit sum for divisibility by 3

The known digit sum is 19.

\[
19+x\equiv 0\pmod{3}
\]

Use the last-two-digits rule for 4

The last two digits must form a number divisible by 4.

\[
10x+6=56
\]

\[
56\equiv 0\pmod{4}
\]

Combine both conditions

The digit satisfying both tests is 5.

\[
19+x=24
\]

\[
\boxed{5}
\]

Answer
With \(x=5\), the tests for 3 and 4 are both satisfied.
\[
19+5=24
\]
\[
24\equiv 0\pmod{3}
\]
\[
56\equiv 0\pmod{4}
\]
Therefore, the required answer is \(5\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (C).

Common Mistake
Do not solve only the first clue. The final answer must satisfy every condition in the question.

Shortcut

Check 3 from the digit sum and 4 from the last two digits.

\[
x\equiv 5\pmod{3}
\]

\[
10x+6\equiv 0\pmod{4}
\]

\[
\boxed{5}
\]

stem.en: The number \(292x6\) is divisible by \(12\). What is the value of \(x\)?

explanation.en:
Observation
This question mixes more than one number-system idea.

Explanation
We are doing this because each clue reduces the choices for the next clue.

Split the rule for 12

A number divisible by 12 must be divisible by both 3 and 4.

\[
N\equiv 0\pmod{3}
\]

\[
N\equiv 0\pmod{4}
\]

Use the digit sum for divisibility by 3

The known digit sum is 19.

\[
19+x\equiv 0\pmod{3}
\]

Use the last-two-digits rule for 4

The last two digits must form a number divisible by 4.

\[
10x+6=56
\]

\[
56\equiv 0\pmod{4}
\]

Combine both conditions

The digit satisfying both tests is 5.

\[
19+x=24
\]

\[
\boxed{5}
\]

Answer
With \(x=5\), the tests for 3 and 4 are both satisfied.
\[
19+5=24
\]
\[
24\equiv 0\pmod{3}
\]
\[
56\equiv 0\pmod{4}
\]
Therefore, the required answer is \(5\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (C).

Do not solve only the first clue. The final answer must satisfy every condition in the question.

\[

question: What is the remainder when \(7^{41}\) is divided by \(19\)?
explanation:

Explanation

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 3.

\[
7\rightarrow 11\rightarrow 1
\]

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(41-1)\bmod 3+1=2
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 11.

\[
7^{41}\equiv 11\pmod{19}
\]

The 2nd term of the cycle is 11.
Therefore, the required answer is \(11\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (D).

Common Mistake
Do not solve only the first clue. The final answer must satisfy every condition in the question.

First make the base small, then use the power pattern.

\[
p=(41-1)\bmod 3+1=2
\]

\[
7^{41}\equiv 11\pmod{19}
\]

Fast result: \(11\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (D).

ਚੱਕਰ ਦਾ 2ਵਾਂ ਪਦ 11 ਹੈ।
ਇਸ ਲਈ ਸਹੀ ਉੱਤਰ ਵਿਕਲਪ (D) ਹੈ। ਲੋੜੀਂਦਾ ਮੁੱਲ \(11\) ਹੈ।

ਆਮ ਗਲਤੀ
ਅਕਸਰ ਗਲਤੀ ਇਹ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਵਿਦਿਆਰਥੀ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਇੱਕ ਸ਼ਰਤ ਦੇਖ ਕੇ ਉੱਤਰ ਚੁਣ ਲੈਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਅੰਤਿਮ ਉੱਤਰ ਨੂੰ ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਸ਼ਰਤਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਜ਼ਰੂਰ ਮਿਲਾਓ।

ਆਧਾਰ ਇੱਕ ਵਾਰ ਘਟਾ ਕੇ ਚੱਕਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਘਾਤ ਦੀ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਤੇ ਜਾਓ।

\[
p=(41-1)\bmod 3+1=2
\]

\[
7^{41}\equiv 11\pmod{19}
\]

ਛੇਤੀ ਨਤੀਜਾ: \(11\)। ਇਸ ਲਈ ਸਹੀ ਉੱਤਰ ਵਿਕਲਪ (D) ਹੈ।

question: The tens place has \(6\), and all digits add to \(11\). Which number is it?
explanation:
Observation
A missing digit is decided by the number rule given in the question.

Explanation
We are doing this because the right digit must make the whole number satisfy the given rule.

Form the digit-sum equation

\[
6+u=11\Rightarrow u=5
\]

Write the two-digit number

Hence, the number is 65.

\[
N=10\times 6+5=65
\]

Answer
Digit sum of 65 is 11.
Therefore, the required answer is \(65\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (D).

Common Mistake
Many students stop as soon as they find a digit. Always put the digit back into the whole number and check the rule again.

Shortcut

Find the ones digit from the digit sum, then place it.

\[
u=5
\]

\[
\boxed{65}
\]

Fast result: \(65\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (D).

question: When you divide \(2^{42}\) by \(7\), what remainder do you get?
explanation:
Observation
The question is about what is left after division.

Explanation
We are doing this because numbers with the same remainder move in equal jumps.

Replace the big base by its smaller remainder

\[
2\equiv 2\pmod{7}
\]

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 3.

\[
2\rightarrow 4\rightarrow 1
\]

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(42-1)\bmod 3+1=3
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 1.

\[
2^{42}\equiv 1\pmod{7}
\]

Answer
The 3rd term of the cycle is 1.
Therefore, the required answer is \(1\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (B).

Common Mistake
Do not count from zero blindly. Check whether the lower and upper limits are included in the given range.

Shortcut

First make the base small, then use the power pattern.

\[
p=(42-1)\bmod 3+1=3
\]

\[
2^{42}\equiv 1\pmod{7}
\]

Fast result: \(1\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (B).

\]

\[

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(43-1)\bmod 6+1=1
\]

Read the required remainder

\[
2^{43}\equiv 2\pmod{9}
\]

The 1st term of the cycle is 2.
Therefore, the required answer is \(2\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (C).

\[

\]

\[

\]

Fast result: \(2\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (C).

pa.question: ਬਾਕੀ ਪਤਾ ਕਰੋ: \(2^{43} \div 9\)।
pa.explanation:
ਧਿਆਨ ਕਰੋ
ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਇਹ ਸਮਝੋ ਕਿ ਪ੍ਰਸ਼ਨ ਕਿਸ ਸੰਖਿਆ-ਨਿਯਮ ਵੱਲ ਇਸ਼ਾਰਾ ਕਰ ਰਿਹਾ ਹੈ।

ਸਮਝਾਉਣ
ਇਹ ਕਦਮ ਇਸ ਲਈ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਹੈ ਕਿਉਂਕਿ ਇਸ ਨਾਲ ਪਤਾ ਲੱਗਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਅੱਗੇ ਕਿਹੜੀ ਗਿਣਤੀ ਕਰਨੀ ਹੈ।

ਆਧਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਭਾਜਕ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਘਟਾਓ

\[
2\equiv 2\pmod{9}
\]

ਬਾਕੀ ਚੱਕਰ ਲਿਖੋ

ਚੱਕਰ ਦੀ ਲੰਬਾਈ = 6।

\[
2\rightarrow 4\rightarrow 8\rightarrow 7\rightarrow 5\rightarrow 1
\]

ਚੱਕਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਘਾਤ ਦੀ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਕੱਢੋ

\[
(43-1)\bmod 6+1=1
\]

ਲੋੜੀਂਦਾ ਬਾਕੀ ਪੜ੍ਹੋ

ਇਸ ਲਈ ਬਾਕੀ = 2।

\[
2^{43}\equiv 2\pmod{9}
\]

ਉੱਤਰ
ਚੱਕਰ ਦਾ 1ਵਾਂ ਪਦ 2 ਹੈ।
ਇਸ ਲਈ ਸਹੀ ਉੱਤਰ ਵਿਕਲਪ (C) ਹੈ। ਲੋੜੀਂਦਾ ਮੁੱਲ \(2\) ਹੈ।

ਆਮ ਗਲਤੀ
ਅਕਸਰ ਗਲਤੀ ਇਹ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਵਿਦਿਆਰਥੀ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਇੱਕ ਸ਼ਰਤ ਦੇਖ ਕੇ ਉੱਤਰ ਚੁਣ ਲੈਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਅੰਤਿਮ ਉੱਤਰ ਨੂੰ ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਸ਼ਰਤਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਜ਼ਰੂਰ ਮਿਲਾਓ।

ਛੋਟਾ ਤਰੀਕਾ

ਆਧਾਰ ਇੱਕ ਵਾਰ ਘਟਾ ਕੇ ਚੱਕਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਘਾਤ ਦੀ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਤੇ ਜਾਓ।

\[
p=(43-1)\bmod 6+1=1
\]

\[
2^{43}\equiv 2\pmod{9}
\]

ਛੇਤੀ ਨਤੀਜਾ: \(2\)। ਇਸ ਲਈ ਸਹੀ ਉੱਤਰ ਵਿਕਲਪ (C) ਹੈ।

Observation
Large powers usually repeat their remainders.

Explanation
We are doing this because the repeating pattern lets us avoid a huge power calculation.

Replace the big base by its smaller remainder

\[
2\equiv 2\pmod{9}
\]

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 6.

\[
2\rightarrow 4\rightarrow 8\rightarrow 7\rightarrow 5\rightarrow 1
\]

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(43-1)\bmod 6+1=1
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 2.

\[
2^{43}\equiv 2\pmod{9}
\]

Answer
The 1st term of the cycle is 2.
Therefore, the required answer is \(2\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (C).

Common Mistake
Do not divide the exponent by the divisor. The exponent is matched with the length of the repeating pattern.

Shortcut

First make the base small, then use the power pattern.

\[
p=(43-1)\bmod 6+1=1
\]

\[
2^{43}\equiv 2\pmod{9}
\]

Fast result: \(2\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (C).

\]

आवश्यक शेषफल पढ़ें

अतः शेषफल = 2।

\[
2^{43}\equiv 2\pmod{9}
\]

उत्तर
चक्र का 1वाँ पद 2 है।
अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प (C) है। आवश्यक मान \(2\) है।

अक्सर गलती यह होती है कि विद्यार्थी केवल एक शर्त देखकर उत्तर चुन लेते हैं। अंतिम उत्तर को सभी शर्तों से मिलाकर जरूर देखें।

\[

question: The tens place has \(8\), and all digits add to \(10\). Which number is it?

Observation
The clues are about digits, so place value is the main idea.

Explanation
We are doing this because digit clues become useful only after we attach them to their places.

Form the digit-sum equation

\[
8+u=10\Rightarrow u=2
\]

Write the two-digit number

Hence, the number is 82.

\[
N=10\times 8+2=82
\]

Answer
Digit sum of 82 is 10.
Therefore, the required answer is \(82\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (B).

Do not treat every digit as having the same value. A digit in the tens place and a digit in the units place are not equal in value.

Shortcut

Find the ones digit from the digit sum, then place it.

question: \(1080\) has how many factors in total?
explanation:
Observation
Every divisor is made by choosing some power of each prime.

Explanation
We are doing this because each prime power gives several choices for building a divisor.

Write prime factorization

\[
1080=2^{3}\times 3^{3}\times 5
\]

For each prime power, count all choices from zero up to that exponent

Each exponent contributes one more choice than its value.

\[
d(1080)=(3+1)\times (3+1)\times (1+1)=32
\]

Answer
The number of positive divisors is 32.
Therefore, the required answer is \(32\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (A).

Common Mistake
Do not multiply the exponents directly. Each exponent gives one extra choice because choosing power zero is also allowed.

Shortcut

Multiply (exponent + 1) across all prime powers.

\[
(3+1)\times (3+1)\times (1+1)
\]

Fast result: \(32\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (A).

explanation.en:
Observation
Every divisor is made by choosing some power of each prime.

Explanation
We are doing this because each prime power gives several choices for building a divisor.

Write prime factorization

\[
1080=2^{3}\times 3^{3}\times 5
\]

For each prime power, count all choices from zero up to that exponent

Each exponent contributes one more choice than its value.

\[
d(1080)=(3+1)\times (3+1)\times (1+1)=32
\]

Answer
The number of positive divisors is 32.
Therefore, the required answer is \(32\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (A).

Common Mistake
Do not multiply the exponents directly. Each exponent gives one extra choice because choosing power zero is also allowed.

Shortcut

Multiply (exponent + 1) across all prime powers.

\[
(3+1)\times (3+1)\times (1+1)
\]

Fast result: \(32\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (A).

question: From \(155\) to \(298\), how many numbers divide evenly by \(12\)?
explanation:
Observation
A missing digit is decided by the number rule given in the question.

Explanation
We are doing this because the right digit must make the whole number satisfy the given rule.

Find the first valid multiple

Therefore, the first multiple of 12 greater than 155 is 156.

\[
12\times 13=156
\]

Find the last valid multiple

Therefore, 288 is the greatest multiple of 12 not exceeding 298.

\[
298=12\times 24+10
\]

\[
298-10=288
\]

Count the valid multiples

The multiples form an arithmetic progression with common difference 12.

\[
\frac{288-156}{12}+1=11+1=12
\]

Answer
The total number of multiples is 12.
Hence, there are 12 multiples of 12 in the given range.
Therefore, the required answer is \(12\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (B).

Common Mistake
Many students stop as soon as they find a digit. Always put the digit back into the whole number and check the rule again.

Shortcut

Count multiples using quotient floors on the range limits.

\[
\left\lfloor\frac{298}{12}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\frac{154}{12}\right\rfloor
\]

\[
24-12=12
\]

Fast result: \(12\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (B).

ਇਹ ਕਦਮ ਇਸ ਲਈ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਹੈ ਕਿਉਂਕਿ ਇਸ ਨਾਲ ਪਤਾ ਲੱਗਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਅੱਗੇ ਕਿਹੜੀ ਗਿਣਤੀ ਕਰਨੀ ਹੈ।

ਪਹਿਲਾ ਵੈਧ ਗੁਣਜ ਕੱਢੋ

ਇਸ ਲਈ 155 ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡਾ 12 ਦਾ ਪਹਿਲਾ ਗੁਣਜ 156 ਹੈ।

\[
12\times 13=156
\]

ਆਖਰੀ ਵੈਧ ਗੁਣਜ ਕੱਢੋ

ਇਸ ਲਈ 288, 298 ਤੋਂ ਵੱਧ ਨਾ ਹੋਣ ਵਾਲਾ 12 ਦਾ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡਾ ਗੁਣਜ ਹੈ।

\[
298=12\times 24+10
\]

\[
298-10=288
\]

ਵੈਧ ਗੁਣਜਾਂ ਦੀ ਗਿਣਤੀ ਕਰੋ

ਗੁਣਜ 12 ਦੇ ਸਾਂਝੇ ਅੰਤਰ ਵਾਲੀ ਸਮਾਂਤਰ ਸ਼੍ਰੇਣੀ ਬਣਾਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ।

\[
\frac{288-156}{12}+1=11+1=12
\]

ਉੱਤਰ
ਗੁਣਜਾਂ ਦੀ ਕੁੱਲ ਗਿਣਤੀ 12 ਹੈ।
ਇਸ ਲਈ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਸੀਮਾ ਵਿੱਚ 12 ਦੇ 12 ਗੁਣਜ ਹਨ।
ਇਸ ਲਈ ਸਹੀ ਉੱਤਰ ਵਿਕਲਪ (B) ਹੈ। ਲੋੜੀਂਦਾ ਮੁੱਲ \(12\) ਹੈ।

ਆਮ ਗਲਤੀ
ਅਕਸਰ ਗਲਤੀ ਇਹ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਵਿਦਿਆਰਥੀ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਇੱਕ ਸ਼ਰਤ ਦੇਖ ਕੇ ਉੱਤਰ ਚੁਣ ਲੈਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਅੰਤਿਮ ਉੱਤਰ ਨੂੰ ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਸ਼ਰਤਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਜ਼ਰੂਰ ਮਿਲਾਓ।

ਛੋਟਾ ਤਰੀਕਾ

ਸੀਮਾ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੇ ਭਾਗਫਲ-ਮੂਲਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਗੁਣਜ ਗਿਣੋ।

\[
\left\lfloor\frac{298}{12}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\frac{154}{12}\right\rfloor
\]

\[
24-12=12
\]

ਛੇਤੀ ਨਤੀਜਾ: \(12\)। ਇਸ ਲਈ ਸਹੀ ਉੱਤਰ ਵਿਕਲਪ (B) ਹੈ।

Observation
A missing digit is decided by the number rule given in the question.

Explanation
We are doing this because the right digit must make the whole number satisfy the given rule.

Find the first valid multiple

Therefore, the first multiple of 12 greater than 155 is 156.

\[
12\times 13=156
\]

Find the last valid multiple

Therefore, 288 is the greatest multiple of 12 not exceeding 298.

\[
298=12\times 24+10
\]

\[
298-10=288
\]

Count the valid multiples

The multiples form an arithmetic progression with common difference 12.

\[
\frac{288-156}{12}+1=11+1=12
\]

Answer
The total number of multiples is 12.

\[
24-12=12

question: What is the remainder when \(7^{89}\) is divided by \(9\)?
explanation:
Observation
The question is about what is left after division.

Explanation
We are doing this because numbers with the same remainder move in equal jumps.

Replace the big base by its smaller remainder

\[
7\equiv 7\pmod{9}
\]

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 3.

\[
7\rightarrow 4\rightarrow 1
\]

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(89-1)\bmod 3+1=2
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 4.

\[
7^{89}\equiv 4\pmod{9}
\]

Answer
The 2nd term of the cycle is 4.
Therefore, the required answer is \(4\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (D).

Common Mistake
Do not count from zero blindly. Check whether the lower and upper limits are included in the given range.

Shortcut

First make the base small, then use the power pattern.

\[
p=(89-1)\bmod 3+1=2
\]

\[
7^{89}\equiv 4\pmod{9}
\]

Fast result: \(4\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (D).

stem.en: What is the remainder when \(7^{89}\) is divided by \(9\)?

explanation.en:
Observation
The question is about what is left after division.

Explanation
We are doing this because numbers with the same remainder move in equal jumps.

Replace the big base by its smaller remainder

\[
7\equiv 7\pmod{9}
\]

Write the remainder cycle

Cycle length = 3.

\[
7\rightarrow 4\rightarrow 1
\]

Find where the exponent falls in the repeating pattern

\[
(89-1)\bmod 3+1=2
\]

Read the required remainder

Hence, remainder = 4.

\[
7^{89}\equiv 4\pmod{9}
\]

Answer
The 2nd term of the cycle is 4.
Therefore, the required answer is \(4\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (D).

Common Mistake
Do not count from zero blindly. Check whether the lower and upper limits are included in the given range.

Shortcut

First make the base small, then use the power pattern.

\[
p=(89-1)\bmod 3+1=2
\]

\[
7^{89}\equiv 4\pmod{9}
\]

Fast result: \(4\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (D).

ਧਿਆਨ ਕਰੋ
ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਇਹ ਸਮਝੋ ਕਿ ਪ੍ਰਸ਼ਨ ਕਿਸ ਸੰਖਿਆ-ਨਿਯਮ ਵੱਲ ਇਸ਼ਾਰਾ ਕਰ ਰਿਹਾ ਹੈ।

ਆਧਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਭਾਜਕ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਘਟਾਓ

\[
7\equiv 7\pmod{9}
\]

ਚੱਕਰ ਦੀ ਲੰਬਾਈ = 3।

\[
7\rightarrow 4\rightarrow 1

\[
(89-1)\bmod 3+1=2
\]

ਇਸ ਲਈ ਬਾਕੀ = 4।

\[
7^{89}\equiv 4\pmod{9}

ਚੱਕਰ ਦਾ 2ਵਾਂ ਪਦ 4 ਹੈ।
ਇਸ ਲਈ ਸਹੀ ਉੱਤਰ ਵਿਕਲਪ (D) ਹੈ। ਲੋੜੀਂਦਾ ਮੁੱਲ \(4\) ਹੈ।

question: In the range \(151\) to \(272\), how many integers are divisible by \(15\)?
explanation:
Observation
A missing digit is decided by the number rule given in the question.

Explanation
We are doing this because the right digit must make the whole number satisfy the given rule.

Find the first valid multiple

Therefore, the first multiple of 15 greater than 151 is 165.

\[
15\times 11=165
\]

Find the last valid multiple

Therefore, 270 is the greatest multiple of 15 not exceeding 272.

\[
272=15\times 18+2
\]

\[
272-2=270
\]

Count the valid multiples

The multiples form an arithmetic progression with common difference 15.

\[
\frac{270-165}{15}+1=7+1=8
\]

Answer
The total number of multiples is 8.
Hence, there are 8 multiples of 15 in the given range.
Therefore, the required answer is \(8\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (A).

Common Mistake
Many students stop as soon as they find a digit. Always put the digit back into the whole number and check the rule again.

Shortcut

Count multiples using quotient floors on the range limits.

\[
\left\lfloor\frac{272}{15}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\frac{150}{15}\right\rfloor
\]

\[
18-10=8
\]

Fast result: \(8\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (A).

stepwiseExplanation.en:
Observation
A missing digit is decided by the number rule given in the question.

Explanation
We are doing this because the right digit must make the whole number satisfy the given rule.

Find the first valid multiple

Therefore, the first multiple of 15 greater than 151 is 165.

\[
15\times 11=165
\]

Find the last valid multiple

Therefore, 270 is the greatest multiple of 15 not exceeding 272.

\[
272=15\times 18+2
\]

\[
272-2=270
\]

Count the valid multiples

The multiples form an arithmetic progression with common difference 15.

\[
\frac{270-165}{15}+1=7+1=8
\]

Answer
The total number of multiples is 8.
Hence, there are 8 multiples of 15 in the given range.
Therefore, the required answer is \(8\). Hence, the correct answer is Option (A).

Common Mistake
Many students stop as soon as they find a digit. Always put the digit back into the whole number and check the rule again.

Shortcut

Count multiples using quotient floors on the range limits.

\[
\left\lfloor\frac{272}{15}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\frac{150}{15}\right\rfloor
\]

\[
18-10=8
\]

Fast result: \(8\). Therefore, the correct answer is Option (A).

अवलोकन

व्याख्या
यह कदम इसलिए जरूरी है क्योंकि इसी से पता चलता है कि आगे कौन-सी गणना करनी है।

पहला मान्य गुणज ज्ञात करें

अतः 151 से बड़ा 15 का पहला गुणज 165 है।

\[
15\times 11=165
\]

आखिरी वैध गुणज ज्ञात करें

अतः 270, 272 से अधिक न होने वाला 15 का सबसे बड़ा गुणज है।

\[
272=15\times 18+2
\]

\[
272-2=270
\]

मान्य गुणजों की गिनती करें

गुणज 15 के सामान्य अंतर वाली समांतर श्रेणी बनाते हैं।

\[
\frac{270-165}{15}+1=7+1=8
\]

उत्तर
गुणजों की कुल संख्या 8 है।
अतः दी गई सीमा में 15 के 8 गुणज हैं।
अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प (A) है। आवश्यक मान \(8\) है।

सामान्य गलती
अक्सर गलती यह होती है कि विद्यार्थी केवल एक शर्त देखकर उत्तर चुन लेते हैं। अंतिम उत्तर को सभी शर्तों से मिलाकर जरूर देखें।

शॉर्टकट

सीमा की सीमाओं पर भागफल-मूल्य से गुणज गिनें।

\[
\left\lfloor\frac{272}{15}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\frac{150}{15}\right\rfloor
\]

\[
18-10=8
\]

शीघ्र परिणाम: \(8\)। अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प (A) है।
stepwiseExplanation.pa:
ਧਿਆਨ ਕਰੋ
ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਇਹ ਸਮਝੋ ਕਿ ਪ੍ਰਸ਼ਨ ਕਿਸ ਸੰਖਿਆ-ਨਿਯਮ ਵੱਲ ਇਸ਼ਾਰਾ ਕਰ ਰਿਹਾ ਹੈ।

ਸਮਝਾਉਣ
ਇਹ ਕਦਮ ਇਸ ਲਈ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਹੈ ਕਿਉਂਕਿ ਇਸ ਨਾਲ ਪਤਾ ਲੱਗਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਅੱਗੇ ਕਿਹੜੀ ਗਿਣਤੀ ਕਰਨੀ ਹੈ।

ਪਹਿਲਾ ਵੈਧ ਗੁਣਜ ਕੱਢੋ

ਇਸ ਲਈ 151 ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡਾ 15 ਦਾ ਪਹਿਲਾ ਗੁਣਜ 165 ਹੈ।

\[
15\times 11=165
\]

ਆਖਰੀ ਵੈਧ ਗੁਣਜ ਕੱਢੋ

ਇਸ ਲਈ 270, 272 ਤੋਂ ਵੱਧ ਨਾ ਹੋਣ ਵਾਲਾ 15 ਦਾ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡਾ ਗੁਣਜ ਹੈ।

\[
272=15\times 18+2
\]

\[
272-2=270
\]

ਵੈਧ ਗੁਣਜਾਂ ਦੀ ਗਿਣਤੀ ਕਰੋ

ਗੁਣਜ 15 ਦੇ ਸਾਂਝੇ ਅੰਤਰ ਵਾਲੀ ਸਮਾਂਤਰ ਸ਼੍ਰੇਣੀ ਬਣਾਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ।

\[
\frac{270-165}{15}+1=7+1=8
\]

ਉੱਤਰ
ਗੁਣਜਾਂ ਦੀ ਕੁੱਲ ਗਿਣਤੀ 8 ਹੈ।
ਇਸ ਲਈ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਸੀਮਾ ਵਿੱਚ 15 ਦੇ 8 ਗੁਣਜ ਹਨ।
ਇਸ ਲਈ ਸਹੀ ਉੱਤਰ ਵਿਕਲਪ (A) ਹੈ। ਲੋੜੀਂਦਾ ਮੁੱਲ \(8\) ਹੈ।

ਆਮ ਗਲਤੀ
ਅਕਸਰ ਗਲਤੀ ਇਹ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਵਿਦਿਆਰਥੀ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਇੱਕ ਸ਼ਰਤ ਦੇਖ ਕੇ ਉੱਤਰ ਚੁਣ ਲੈਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਅੰਤਿਮ ਉੱਤਰ ਨੂੰ ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਸ਼ਰਤਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਜ਼ਰੂਰ ਮਿਲਾਓ।

ਛੋਟਾ ਤਰੀਕਾ

ਸੀਮਾ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੇ ਭਾਗਫਲ-ਮੂਲਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਗੁਣਜ ਗਿਣੋ।

\[
\left\lfloor\frac{272}{15}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\frac{150}{15}\right\rfloor
\]

\[
18-10=8
\]

ਛੇਤੀ ਨਤੀਜਾ: \(8\)। ਇਸ ਲਈ ਸਹੀ ਉੱਤਰ ਵਿਕਲਪ (A) ਹੈ।
